headline: Canada reimposes sanctions on 11 Iranian entities at the G7 Paris meeting
dek: [VERIFIED FACT -- the measures] Canada reimposed sanctions on 11 Iranian entities on Tuesday Nov 10 for contributing to Iran's nuclear activities and ballistic missile program (Reuters; AFP; Global Affairs Canada). Foreign Minister Anita Anand announced the measures at the G7 foreign ministers'…
sources: Global Affairs Canada statement (Minister Anita Anand, Paris); Reuters; AFP
fault_line: Sanctions as leverage or sanctions as punishment -- does re-listing Iran's oil company, tanker company and biggest banks push Tehran to the table, or just close the door on the deal?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the measures] Canada reimposed sanctions on 11 Iranian entities on Tuesday Nov 10 for contributing to Iran's nuclear activities and ballistic missile program (Reuters; AFP; Global Affairs Canada). Foreign Minister Anita Anand announced the measures at the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris, saying they were intended to restrict Iran's access to funding and sensitive technology linked to its nuclear and missile programs. [VERIFIED FACT -- the list] The 11 entities: Nuclear Fuel Production and Procurement Company; Nuclear Reactors Fuel Company; Kala Naft; Naftiran Intertrade Company; National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC); National Iranian Tanker Company (NITC); Bank Mellat; Bank Melli Iran; Bank of Industry and Mine; Export Development Bank of Iran; Iran Insurance Company. [VERIFIED FACT -- the reversal] Canada delisted these entities in 2016 in recognition of Iran's progress under the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA); the measures are reimposed under Canada's Special Economic Measures (Iran) Regulations. [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- the position] Anand: 'Canada's position is unequivocal: Iran must never be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon' (AFP); Canada says it remains eager to work with partners toward a sustainable agreement on Iran's nuclear program. [CONTEXT] The announcement coincides with the G7 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Paris and follows France's move the same day to seek EU sanctions against Iran over the IRGC supermarket-fridge cyberattack (recorded at 1400-02).
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct tiered publisher families: Reuters (T1) + AFP (T1) + Global Affairs Canada (T1, STATE CA -- the primary source itself, announcing its own measures).
sections.what_disputed: (a) Scale: a Canada-only re-listing of 11 entities -- material to Iran's oil/shipping/banking plumbing, but not a new multilateral sanctions regime; no other G7 member has announced matching measures today. (b) The measures restore a 2016 status quo rather than adding new designations; their practical bite depends on enforcement and on whether Iranian oil/shipping counterparties deal with Canada at all. (c) No Iranian response on record at last check.
sections.why_matters: Canada just unwound the 2016 sanctions relief in the middle of the war -- re-listing Iran's oil company, its tanker company and its biggest banks. The target list is the exact plumbing that moves Iran's oil. And it was announced at the G7 table in Paris.

totw_analysis: Our read: Canada just unwound the 2016 sanctions relief in the middle of the war -- re-listing Iran's oil company, its tanker company and its biggest banks. The target list is the exact plumbing that moves Iran's oil. And it was announced at the G7 table in Paris. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Sanctions as leverage or sanctions as punishment -- does re-listing Iran's oil company, tanker company and biggest banks push Tehran to the table, or just close the door on the deal?
